item.description: CUDA: split the PAD_REFLECT_1D grid to stay within the HIP grid limit (#32179) The kernel launches one block per row and 256-wide tile, so the {2, 16777217} test case asks for 16777217 blocks of 256 threads. HIP refuses a grid dimension above 2^32 threads and the ROCm jobs fail with "invalid configuration argument". The host now launches the grid in chunks of at most UINT32_MAX / 256 blocks and passes the chunk offset to the kernel. item.description: CUDA: skip empty MoE tiles in MMQ stream-k fixup (#32067) * CUDA: skip empty MoE tiles in MMQ stream-k fixup mul_mat_q_stream_k_fixup loads ids_dst[col_low + j] for all j < J before checking j_sup. mul_mat_q returns early on col_low == col_high, the fixup kernel did not. mm_ids_helper emits one extra tile per expert that may be empty; for trailing experts col_low == ncols_dst, so the load reads one element past the J_best-1 padding added in #29953. The kernel returns at j >= j_sup before storing anything, so results are unaffected. Return early when j_sup <= 0, like the main kernel. The return is block-uniform (tsj is loaded once per block) and precedes __syncthreads(). item.description: ui: keep downloads in Discover during search and fix their progress with a draft (#31467) * ui : keep downloads in Discover sidebar during search, sort base-org repos first - Show the sticky Downloading section regardless of an active search query - Order search results so repos published by their base model's org lead Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium) * server : throttle download progress per file Files of a download run in parallel threads, but progress updates were throttled with one shared timer. A small draft sidecar reports far more often than the main weights, so it took nearly every slot and the main file's updates, including the first one carrying its total size, were dropped until the draft finished. The UI then showed the draft's progress first and restarted from 0% for the model. Throttle each file on its own and always pass a file's first update. Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium) * ui: list a downloading repo once and match base orgs case-insensitively A search hit that is downloading already shows under Downloading, so the results leave it out. Base model orgs compare without case, as the hub treats them. Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium) * server : tell clients a download stopped on request When a client paused or cancelled a download, every other client following /models/sse got a bare download_failed and could not tell it from an error, so the web UI showed "Download failed" for a pause made in the Llama app. A stop asked for through unload or delete now fails with {"stopped": true}. Deleting a paused download, which has no instance left, now sends model_remove as deleting a running one does, so other clients drop its row. Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium) * ui : follow downloads other clients start, pause or cancel A download another client started (e.g. the Llama app) already showed up from the feed; it now also picks up the sidecars the list reports for it. A stop another client asked for reads as a pause instead of a failure, and a removal clears the download row even when the list does not carry it yet. item.description: cuda : use MMVF for BF16 matrices of few rows at small batch sizes (#31959) MMF tiles 32 rows per block, so a BF16 matrix with few rows (e.g. the qwen4exp hyper-connection projections, 320 rows with K = 10240) runs only a handful of blocks and leaves most SMs idle at batch sizes 2..8. MMVF runs a block per row and wins there when K is long enough. MMVF's cost grows with rows x batch while MMF's stays roughly flat in that range, so use MMVF only while rows * ne11 * 256 <= nsm * min(K, max_k) and K >= 1024. The budget scales with the SM count, which keeps GPUs with few SMs (e.g. the A16) on MMF. Blackwell allows up to 8 columns and max_k = 6144; older GPUs stop at 5 columns and max_k = 4096. Add eval cases at 128x2560, 512x2560 and 320x10240 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu 24.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: vulkan: add tiled-transpose concat shader for Qwen models (#30591) * vulkan: tiled transpose for dim-0 concat with a transposed source The delta-net conv-state path does ggml_transpose() straight into a dim-0 ggml_concat(), so the generic concat kernel reads src1 with the transposed stride, one element per thread, and neighbouring lanes land on different cache lines. Stage a 32x32 tile through shared memory instead, which keeps both the load and the store coalesced. 33 columns pads away the bank conflicts. Gated narrowly: dim 0, 2D, unquantized 4-byte elements, contiguous src0/dst rows, and src1 actually transposed. Everything else falls through to the existing kernel. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on gfx1151/RADV, 30 gated-delta-net layers: the CONCAT op goes 11877 us -> 957 us, and pp2048 at ub2048 goes 1224 -> 1628 t/s. Generated text is unchanged. item.description: ggml-rpc : fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed handshakes (#30415) * ggml-rpc: fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed handshakes rpc_dispatcher::start() aborted the whole process (GGML_ABORT -> SIGABRT) when the endpoint could not be parsed, the transport failed to initialise, the socket could not connect, or the HELLO handshake failed. A typo in --rpc or a temporarily down node killed the host application, and the reason went to a log stream the host may never see. Make the connect-time failure reportable instead of fatal: start() returns bool (LOG_ERROR + false; the dispatcher thread only starts after a successful handshake), negotiate_hello() returns false on a half-open socket, get_dispatcher() returns nullptr and does not cache failed attempts, and every consumer treats nullptr as "endpoint did not answer" with the conservative behaviour of its domain (allocation -> nullptr, alloc-size -> lower bound, device memory -> 0/0, events -> no-op, device count -> 0, and add_server() already maps 0 devices to nullptr). item.description: vulkan: cap scalar flash attention at 8 rows for large heads on Qualcomm (#30829) With head sizes above 128 and KV >= 1024, scalar flash attention uses 16 rows per workgroup. On the Qualcomm Adreno driver this variant spills registers to scratch memory (264 bytes per invocation on the X1-85, none at 8 rows) and runs about 40x slower. The largest test-backend-ops case then becomes a single dispatch of several seconds, past the Windows GPU timeout, and the test never completes on the X1 Elite. Use at most 8 rows per workgroup on Qualcomm when hsk or hsv > 128. Smaller heads keep 16 rows, which is faster for them on the X2 Elite. Adreno X1-85, FLASH_ATTN_EXT hsk=256 kv=4096: nb=64 711 ms -> 17 ms, nb=512 no result -> 125 ms; test-backend-ops completes. item.description: ggml : update CUDA/Metal radix Top-K to make tied selections deterministic (#31084) * ggml : fix for the radix TOP_K thread timing bug * make the key an ordered 64-bit pair * a rewrite without shift-skip logic * fix casts * warp-contiguous layout * reduce the scope removing vulkan+metal changes * turn it off for Metal/ROCm, note about cub::DeviceTopK * fix the hip build * skip Vulkan as well * popc lambda from fattn * do block_cols math in int64_t * make it allowlist bc SYCL looks non deterministic too * ggml : make Metal radix Top-K tied selections deterministic The radix top-k kernel gathered the selected indices with atomic counters, so the order of the tied candidates at the threshold (and, with more ties than remaining slots, the subset itself) depended on the thread scheduling. Replace the two atomic compaction loops with a deterministic scheme: count the elements above and tied with the threshold in contiguous per-thread chunks, rank them with a simdgroup scan and a serial scan over the (now unused) radix histogram, and write each kept element exactly once in column order. The output is now byte-identical across runs. This is also faster than the atomic version: the strided atomic loops become contiguous passes, reducing top-k times by ~20-45% on M5 Ultra, with tie-heavy shapes within a few percent. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * tests : enable deterministic top-k check on Metal, add radix-path tie cases Metal now produces deterministic tied selections for the radix top-k path, so the determinism self-check runs for the MTL backend as well. Add eval cases covering the radix path (ncols > 2048) with more ties at the threshold than remaining slots, and tie-heavy perf cases to monitor the cost of the deterministic tie handling. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * ggml : use coalesced accesses in the Metal radix Top-K compaction The deterministic compaction walked contiguous per-thread chunks with scalar sequential loads, which the memory system of the M2 Ultra can not overlap well: the radix Top-K times regressed by ~1.5-2.4x on the large-ncols shapes. Give each warp a contiguous chunk of the row instead and let the lanes interleave within it with stride 32, so every access is fully coalesced. The lanes write their kept elements at lane-major ranks, which is deterministic, and only a tie overflow falls back to a per-step cross-lane ranking to keep the lowest tied indices in column order. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * tests : remove the extra top-k tie and perf cases The radix-path eval and tie-heavy perf cases were added to validate and benchmark the Metal deterministic tie handling. item.description: llama_moe_cache: run missed experts on CPU, add tuning script (#30966) * moe-cache : compute part of the misses on the CPU --moe-cache-cpu-share F computes a share F of the MoE cache misses on the CPU from the host experts instead of uploading them. The graph builds the expert FFN twice: on the device from the cache slots, where the misses left to the CPU read zero slots, and on the CPU from the host experts, where the experts computed on the device have id -1. The two results are added before the down bias. - ggml-cpu: MUL_MAT_ID skips negative ids and writes zero rows - sched: the copy callback is called for all the inputs of a split, and before the host sync when there are no events - the slot lookup callback reads the inputs of the CPU part together with the selected experts, so the CPU part does not wait for the device, and its result is copied back asynchronously - each token uses distinct zero slots, mul_mat_id does not support an expert selected twice by a token - LLAMA_MOE_CACHE_TRACE writes the selected experts of each lookup, for a simulator of the cache * scripts : add moe-cache-tune.py to pick the MoE cache arguments The script wraps a llama-server command: it starts the server at two cache sizes and three CPU shares, fits the upload and CPU speeds of the machine, and replays the routing of the runs through a copy of the cache logic to predict other sizes and shares. It prints the recommended --moe-cache-mib and --moe-cache-cpu-share. docs/moe-cache.md describes the MoE cache arguments and the script. * add am17an as codeowner for MoE cache * moe-cache : upload all the misses until the cache is full With a high --moe-cache-cpu-share, few misses are uploaded, so an empty cache fills slowly and more misses than needed go to the CPU. The CPU share now starts once all the slots of a cache group hold an expert. moe-cache-tune.py replays the same rule. * add backend sync for async transfer queue * moe-cache : let the scheduler copy the results of the CPU part * Fix MSVC compilation * remove sync change * llama-graph : extract the CPU share condition into can_cpu_share * llama-graph : make llm_graph_params::moe_cache const The graph construction no longer updates the MoE cache directly: the CPU parts of the layers are accumulated in the graph result and applied to the cache in llama_context::process_ubatch, after the graph inputs are set and before the graph is computed. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * scripts : replay the ClassLRU policy in moe-cache-tune.py * moe-cache : pick CPU misses by CRF instead of random (#31853) * moe-cache : remove the backend logic of the CPU part from the graph The CPU part reads the host experts, so the scheduler places it on the CPU without set_tensor_backend. The cache gives no CPU map for batches that a device would offload. Graphs with a CPU part look up their own slot map, so the graph does not register the part with the cache. ggml-backend : the inputs of the next split that are already computed are copied to host memory before the current split runs, so a CPU split does not wait for the device split before it. This replaces the stash of the cache, and the copy callback is again called for host weights only. * llama-graph : return the MoE cache slots and CPU ids in a struct The scheduler prefetch no longer checks that the next split runs on another backend: the inputs of a split are never on its own backend, so the input loop already skips that case. --------- Co-authored-by: Gaurav Garg Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov Co-authored-by: Alexey Kopytko **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: metal : fix GROUP_NORM for ne03 > 1 and non-contiguous inputs (#31852) The kernel_group_norm_f32 kernel and its host dispatch ignored the batch dimension (ne03) of the source tensor: only ngrp threadgroups were dispatched and each normalized the flat range [tgpig*gs, (tgpig+1)*gs) with gs = ne00*ne01*ceil(ne02/ngrp). For tensors with ne03 > 1, all but the first ne00*ne01*ne02 elements were left unwritten (exposed by the new GROUP_NORM test with ne=[3,1,1,65537], num_groups=1). Dispatch one threadgroup per (group, i03) pair (ngrp in x, ne03 in z, same work distribution as the Vulkan backend) and compute per-batch statistics, matching the CPU reference. Also clamp the group element count for the last group when ne02 is not divisible by ngrp and use int64_t indexing. The kernel now only requires ggml_is_contiguous_rows(op->src[0]) instead of full contiguity: it addresses src0 and dst with their own strides (nb03 and the dst strides are added to the kernel args - dst can be a strided view of src0 with ggml_group_norm_inplace) and falls back from the flat fast path to a strided path that decodes the linear element index when rows or channels are padded. The flat/strided selection is done on the host in ggml_metal_library_get_pipeline_group_norm and compiled into one of two specialized pipeline variants via a FC_group_norm_flat function constant, so the dead path is eliminated at pipeline creation. GROUP_NORM support is also gated on F32 src and dst in supports_op - the kernel only implements f32 and an f16 input would silently be read as f32. item.description: server: visit parent slots before child slots (#30779) * server: visit parent slots before child slots A parent slot wakes its waiting child slots once it finishes the shared prompt prefix, while slots are visited in id order. When a child task lands on a lower slot id than its parent, the child is visited before the parent wakes it and waits an extra batch to process its suffix. Non-child slots are now visited before active child slots, so every child woken by its parent joins the same batch. * server: check systemone test events through test tags The systemone tests matched free-form debug messages, including the formatted f_keep value of the prompt cache. The server now emits __TEST_TAG_WAIT_PARENT_SLOT__ when a child slot waits for its parent, __TEST_TAG_PROMPT_CACHE_RESTORE__ on every prompt cache restore and __TEST_TAG_PROMPT_CACHE_FULL_RESTORE__ when the whole cached prompt is a prefix of the new one, compared on token counts. --------- Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI
